problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-6{e}^{-2t}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. Question 2

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=−6e−2t, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=2m/s when t=0s, find the velocity (in m/s) of the particle at time t.

a
 v(t)=12e−t−10
b
 v(t)=−2e−2t+4
c
v(t)=3e−2t−1
d
 v(t)=3e−2t+2
e
 v(t)=−2e−t+2
